ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is an AC voltage source, labeled 10 sin(ωt), with frequency f = 50 Hz. The upper end of the source is connected through a series ideal diode to the load node on the right; on the right there is a 1 kΩ resistor connected to the lower return loop. The output V0 is marked across this resistor, with the upper end positive and the lower end negative. The diode direction makes it conduct toward the load during the positive half-cycle of the input. Reasoning: Ignoring the diode voltage drop, during the positive half-cycle 0 < ωt < π, the diode conducts, so v0(t) = 10 sin(ωt). During the negative half-cycle π < ωt < 2π, the diode is cut off, and the load voltage v0(t) = 0. Therefore this is a half-wave rectified waveform. The reading of an average-type DC voltmeter is the one-period average value: Vavg = (1/(2π)) ∫_0^π 10 sinθ dθ = (10/(2π))[-cosθ]_0^π = (10/(2π))(2) = 10/π ≈ 3.18 V.
